question: Under the proposed National Building Research Institute law, how long does an employee have to decide whether to decline the offered position after being notified?
answer:
The evidence supports **six months**: an officer or employee who wishes to opt out "may do so within six months from the date on which he was offered employment in the Institute" [629/2025 §33(2)(b)] — the same text appears in the Gazette version, "National Building Research Institute - GS" [621/2025 §33(2)(b)].

- The newest version is the Bill presented 2025-08-19 (629/2025); the GS version is dated 2025-07-17, and the two are identical here.
- Non-acceptance also triggers compensation under a voluntary retirement scheme, approved by the Minister and the Minister of Finance [629/2025 §33(2)(c)].

Caveats: The evidence supplied for §33 may be truncated; if a separate provision fixes a different period for deciding on the offer, it is not in this corpus.

question: Under the proposed Inland Revenue amendment, from which assessment date are deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act excluded from subsection (2)?
answer:
Deductions previously claimed under sections 32, 33 or 34 of the repealed Act are excluded from subsection (2) for any year of assessment "prior to April 1, 2018" [013/2026 §37].

- The exclusion applies even if an un-deducted balance of that deduction still remains as at April 1, 2018 [013/2026 §37].
- Text is from the Inland Revenue (Amendment) bill, GS version dated 2026-02-24, inserting new section 202(2A); the passage notes identical text in 022/2026 [013/2026 §37].

question: Under the proposed Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority law, how long does a licence issued or renewed remain in effect?
answer:
Under the Microfinance and Credit Regulatory Authority Bill (645/2025, GS 2025-11-17; identical text in 653/2025) the answer differs by licence type.

- A moneylending licence issued under s.23 or renewed under s.24 is "valid for a period of one year" and must "specify the date of expiry" [645/2025 §25(c),(d)].
- A licence to carry on the microfinance business "shall be issued for a period of three years" [645/2025 §32(7)].
- Consistently, s.32(9) applies s.24 and s.25 paragraphs (a), (b), (d) and (e) to microfinance licences — omitting the one-year rule in paragraph (c) [645/2025 §32(9)].

Caveats: §25 expressly covers licences "issued under section 23 or renewed under section 24"; the three-year term appears only for microfinance business licences.

question: How far in advance must a container depot operator lodge a renewal request before the current licence ends?
answer:
At least **30 days before** the current licence expires: the renewal application must be submitted “not less than thirty days prior to the date of expiration of the licence previously issued” [657/2025 §6].

- It must be in the prescribed Form and accompanied by the prescribed renewal fee [657/2025 §6].
- The same §6 text is stated to be identical in Bill 007/2026 (2026-01-20) [657/2025 §6].

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, what is the new maximum duration a freezing order may be in effect?
answer:
The newest version is Bill 033/2026 (Bill, 2026-05-05); the GS version 020/2026 (2026-03-17) has identical text. The order itself runs "for a period of fourteen working days" (up from seven) [033/2026 §8], while the outer limit in section 8(2)(b) rises from "a period of two years" to "a period of three years" [033/2026 §9].

- Per-extension cap in the High Court subsection: "shall not exceed three months" replaced by "shall not exceed four months" [033/2026 §9].
- Power to issue the order sits with a police officer "not below the rank of an Assistant Superintendent of Police" [033/2026 §8].

Caveats: the question's "maximum duration" could mean the 14-working-day order or the multi-year extension ceiling — the evidence supports both figures, but the clauses are shown only as substitutions, not with the surrounding subsection (2) wording.

question: Under the amended Telecommunication Levy law, how often is the levy calculated on the value of telecom services received?
answer:
Monthly: the levy is charged "on the value of the supply of telecommunication services ... in respect of each month" [028/2026 §2].

- It is levied from "every person receiving any telecommunication service" at rates in the Schedule [028/2026 §2].
- Same text appears in the presented Bill 035/2026 (2026-05-06); the GS version 028/2026 is dated 2026-04-23 [035/2026 §2].
- Diplomatic Privileges Act No. 9 of 1996 persons/organisations are exempt [028/2026 §2].

Caveats: The Schedule of rates is referenced only, not quoted in the evidence.

question: Under the amended Bills of Exchange Ordinance, what ways are allowed for informing a party that a bill has been refused or not paid?
answer:
The amended section 49(5) allows notice of dishonour to be given "in writing or by personal communication, or by facsimile transmission or other electronic means" which sufficiently identify the bill and intimate that it has been dishonoured by non-acceptance or non-payment [601/2025 §8].

- It replaces the existing subsection (5) of section 49 of the principal enactment [601/2025 §8].
- The same wording appears in the other versions: 612/2025 (Bill, 2025-06-17), 527/2024 and 552/2024 [601/2025 §8].

Caveats: The clause text is quoted from the GS version 601/2025 (2025-06-04); the labels state it is identical in 612/2025, but no separate clause text for 612/2025 is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation incorporation law, who is defined as a qualified auditor?
answer:
The evidence passage labelled as the Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation (Incorporation) Bill defines a "qualified auditor" as either an individual member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka (or any other Institute established by law) holding "a certified to practice as Accountant issued by the Council of such Institute", or a firm of accountants whose resident partners each hold that membership and certificate [626/2025 §11(4)].

- The same clause says accounts "shall be audited by a qualified auditor appointed by Auditor General in terms of Article 154 of the Constitution" [626/2025 §11(3)].
- Text quoted verbatim, including the apparent typo "a certified to practice" [626/2025 §11(4)(a)].

Caveats: this passage is expressly "identical text also in 607/2025", i.e. generic boilerplate; no independent passage confirms the Kodhagoda Gunarathana Nahimi Foundation bill's own audit clause, so the bill-specific definition cannot be confirmed from this corpus.

question: What is meant by “knowledge sharing activities” under the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture Act?
answer:
Under [646/2025 §18] (interpretation section), “knowledge sharing activities” means “activities designed to facilitate to exchange of ideas, skills, and experiences fostering on culture of learning and collaboration”.

- It covers exchange of three things: “ideas, skills, and experiences”, aimed at a “culture of learning and collaboration” [646/2025 §18].
- Source: the Sri Lanka Institute of Agriculture (Incorporation) bill, GS version dated 2025-11-20, p.15; identical text appears in 002/2026 [646/2025 §18].

Caveats: The quoted wording contains apparent drafting errors (“facilitate to exchange”, “fostering on culture”); the title also includes “(Incorporation)”.

question: According to the proposed Pharmaceutical Society of Sri Lanka law, what authority does the Society have to obtain and manage real or personal assets, and what actions may it take with those assets?
answer:
Under the newest version, Bill 047/2026 (25 June 2026), the Society may “take and hold any property, movable or immovable” vested by purchase, grant, gift, testamentary disposition or otherwise, held for the Act’s purposes and subject to s7 rules; it may “sell, mortgage, lease, exchange, or otherwise dispose of” that property [047/2026 §13].

- It may “purchase, rent construct, renovate and otherwise obtain lands or buildings” and deal with/dispose of them as the Council determines to promote its objects [047/2026 §6(a)].
- It may administer a lawful trust with similar objects or “any real or personal property” to promote its objects [047/2026 §6(f)].
- Rules must cover “administration and management of the property” [047/2026 §7(f)]; the GS 041/2026 (11 June 2026) wording is the same [041/2026 §13].

question: In the Institute of Real Estate Professionals, who chairs the Membership and Policy Advisory committees, and how are chairs selected for the remaining committees?
answer:
The President of the Institute chairs both — the proviso to §18(2) makes the President "the Chairman of the Committees referred to in paragraphs (a) and (b)" of subsection (1), i.e. the Membership Committee and the Policy Advisory and Constitutional Committee [656/2025 §18(2)]. For the remaining committees, each must include at least one Council member, and that member is Chairman [656/2025 §18(2)]; if more than one Council member is appointed, "the Council shall appoint one of such members as the Chairperson" [656/2025 §18(3)].

- Same rule in the earlier GS version, 637/2025 (2025-10-01), text identical; the Bill version is 656/2025 (2025-12-05) [656/2025 §18; 637/2025 §18].
- In a Chairperson's absence, members present elect one of themselves to preside [656/2025 §18(5)].

Caveats: the passage is truncated at the proviso's end, so nothing further on these committees is in evidence; composition/powers are left to rules under the Act [656/2025 §18(4)].

question: Under the amended Colombo Port City Economic Commission law, how is the income tax treatment of workers hired by licensed businesses affected depending on whether the licence was granted before or after the new provisions take effect?
answer:
Under the newest version, **Bill 654/2025 (Bill, 5 Dec 2025; same text as GS 652/2025, 28 Nov 2025)**, workers of businesses licensed **before** the replacement section 35 commences get a three-year income-tax exemption; workers of businesses licensed **on or after** that date are liable to income tax. [654/2025 §3]

- Pre-commencement licence holders may employ residents or non-residents paid in a “designated foreign currency”, and for “a period of three years” resident and non-resident employment income is “exempt from income tax”. [654/2025 §3]
- Post-commencement licence holders: resident and non-resident employment income “shall be liable to income tax”. [654/2025 §3]

Caveats: The GS and Bill versions are materially identical on this point. [652/2025 §3]

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Licensing of Shipping Agents, Freight Forwarders, Non‑Vessel Operating Common Carriers and Container Operators Act, how is the Act’s long title changed regarding the mention of container operators?
answer:
The long title is amended by deleting the words “and container operators”, so the list ends at “freight forwarders and non-vessel operating common carriers”. [658/2025 §2]

- The substitution replaces “freight forwArders, non-VesseL operAting common cArriers, And contAiner operAtors” with “freight forwArders And non-VesseL operAting common cArriers”. [658/2025 §2]
- The same §2 text appears in Bill 005/2026 (presented 2026-01-20) as in the GS version 658/2025 (2025-12-12). [005/2026; 658/2025 §2]
- Relatedly, §3(1) substitutes the full short title, dropping “and Container Operators” in favour of “…Non-Vessel Operating Common Carriers Act”. [658/2025 §3]

Caveats: My answer is based on §2 of the GS bill 658/2025, which the evidence says is identical in 005/2026; the long title wording itself is quoted only at §2.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, what modification is being made to the existing law?
answer:
The amendment rewrites the Convention on the Suppression of Terrorist Financing Act, No. 25 of 2005 by substituting defined terms throughout the Act per a Schedule, and by broadening its offences, reach and penalties (newest text: Bill 029/2026, 2026-04-09; an earlier GS version 018/2026, 2026-03-11, carries identical wording in the passages cited).

- It extends the Act to acts "wholly or partly outside Sri Lanka" directed at Sri Lanka, its citizens, a government facility, or to compel the Government [029/2026 §3].
- New offences cover organizing/directing, abetting, and collecting or providing funds even where not "actually used" or linked to a specific act, including for terrorist training, travel or becoming a "foreign terrorist fighter" [029/2026 §4].
- "Funds or property" is redefined as "funds, property or other assets" throughout the Act, with new definitions such as "armed conflict" and "foreign terrorist fighter" [018/2026 §16; 029/2026 p.20].

Caveats: Penalties (fine up to 100 million rupees) and notice periods (7 days to 14 working days) appear only in the auto-generated summaries, not in the clause text supplied — verify against the bill.

question: Which 2025 bill outlines the government's budget and borrowing provisions for the financial year 2026?
answer:
Both **632/2025** and **639/2025** are Appropriation bills for financial year 2026, with identical §2 text; the newest is **639/2025 (Bill, 2025-09-26)**, alongside **632/2025 (Other, 2025-09-17)**.

- Long title: "to provide for the service of the financial year 2026; to authorize the raising of loans in or outside Sri Lanka" [639/2025].
- §2(1): expenditure of "rupees four thousand four hundred thirty-four billion three hundred fifty-six million four hundred sixty-eight thousand" for 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026, met from the Consolidated Fund and from borrowing capped at "rupees three thousand eight hundred billion", loan details in the Final Budget Position Report under s.51 of the Public Financial Management Act, No. 44 of 2024 [639/2025 §2].

Caveats: Evidence quotes §2 and the long title only; clauses beyond §10 and the schedules are not verifiable, and it does not say which of the two versions supersedes the other.

question: What 2026 legislation establishes a new foundation to promote economic growth and rural resource development in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Economic and Rural Resources Development Foundation (Incorporation)** bill — Bill 055/2026, presented 27 July 2026 (Gazette version 043/2026, 15 June 2026).

- It incorporates the existing Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession, able to sue, be sued and use a common seal [043/2026 §2(1)].
- Objects include contributing to national and social development "by developing, promoting, establishing, expanding or modernising all economic sectors in Sri Lanka" [043/2026 §3(1)(a)], plus rural youth vocational training and empowerment of rural, estate and underserved communities [043/2026 §3(1)(b), (h)].
- Objects must be carried out "without any distinction based on race, religion, language, caste, sex, political opinion, place of birth" [043/2026 §3(2)].

Caveats: the presented bill's title spells "Recourses"; no penalties are set out.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media law, what is the maximum length of a suspension the Council can impose instead of disenrolling a member?
answer:
One year — the Council may, "in lieu of disenrolling a member," "suspend him from membership for such period not exceeding one year" [054/2026 §24].

- This power arises where the Disciplinary Committee's report establishes "professional misconduct" [054/2026 §24], as defined by Council rules [054/2026 §23 §2].
- Less severe alternatives listed are to "warn, reprimand or suspend" [054/2026 §24].
- The Council may also re-enroll the person at its discretion [054/2026 §24].

Caveats: The title in the evidence is "Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media - Bill" (2026-07-22); identical text appears in 040/2026 and 050/2026 (dates not given).

question: Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, how long must someone have continuously and peacefully occupied a premises to be regarded as an “occupant”?
answer:
Under the Protection of Occupants Bill, a person qualifies as an "occupant" if they are in lawful occupation and have had "undisturbed and uninterrupted occupation" of the premises "for a period of more than three months" before the events in sections 3, 4 or 5 [004/2026 §2].

- The same threshold appears in the earlier Gazette version, Bill 634/2025 (GS, 2025-09-18) [634/2025 §2].
- The wording is "more than three months" — not three months exactly — and requires both lawful and undisturbed/uninterrupted occupation [004/2026 §2].

Caveats: only §2 was supplied; no later committee-stage changes are in this corpus.

question: Under the proposed Gambling Regulatory Authority law, what is the age limit beyond which a person cannot serve on the Authority's Board?
answer:
A person is disqualified from appointment to the Board if they "is over seventy years of age" — i.e. the cut-off is 70 [613/2025 §9(i)].

- This appears as one of the disqualifications in the Bill presented on 2025-06-17; the same clause text is noted as identical in the earlier Gazette version 594/2025 (2025-05-27) [613/2025 §9, §9(i)].
- Board composition itself (ex-officio members plus three Minister-appointed members) is set out separately and does not mention age [594/2025 §7(3)].

Caveats: the evidence shows disqualification from *appointment*; it does not quote a separate provision on removal or continuation in office on reaching 70.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Financial Transactions Reporting Act, what is the longest jail term a person can receive for arriving in or departing Sri Lanka with cash or bearer‑negotiable instruments above the minister‑set limit?
answer:
One year: imprisonment "of either description for a term not exceeding one year," on conviction by a Magistrate [021/2026 §31]. The operative provision is the substituted section 27; the fine may be up to "three times of the value of the cash or bearer negotiable instruments," or both fine and imprisonment [021/2026 §31].

- The excess cash or instruments are also forfeited to the State [021/2026 §31].
- Same maximum applies where the sum is specified by the Minister under the Foreign Exchange Act, No. 12 of 2017 [021/2026 §31].
- The older 2005 provision carried the same one-year maximum but a lower fine cap, "one hundred thousand rupees" [020/2005 §27].

Caveats: the evidence is the Gazette version (GS, 2026-03-17) of the bill titled "Financial Transactions Reporting (Amendment)," which amends the Financial Transactions Reporting Act rather than being that Act; identical text also appears in 030/2026. No presented Bill version is in evidence.

question: Under the proposed Sri Lanka Cricket law, what penalty amount does a member owe if they fail to pay the subscription by the deadline?
answer:
Under the Sri Lanka Cricket bill, a defaulting member owes a "late payment fee equal to twice the annual subscription", payable by "the thirtieth day of April of the following year" [072/2026 §30(4)].

- The subscription itself was due "on or before the thirty first day of December of the year immediately preceding the relevant year" [072/2026 §30(3)].
- Missing the later date too means automatic forfeiture of voting rights [072/2026 §30(5)], and removal from the Register of Members after six months from the due date [072/2026 §30(6)].

Caveats: This is the GS version ("Sri Lanka Cricket - GS", 2026-09-28); identical text appears in 077/2026 but I have not verified differences from a presented Bill.

question: Under the proposed Indira Cancer Charitable Trust Act, on which day must the newly formed body corporate settle the Trust's existing debts and liabilities?
answer:
The text fixes *which* debts are covered, not a deadline: debts and liabilities "existing on the day immediately preceding the date of commencement of this Act" must be paid by the body corporate, with no date or time limit for payment stated [009/2026 §12].

- Newest match is the Indira Cancer Charitable Trust (Incorporation) bill, GS dated 2026-02-05, p.11, with identical text in 014/2026 [009/2026 §12].
- The near-identical 2021 bill, "Indira Cancer Trust (Incorporation)" (GS 2021-08-23), uses the same wording [095/2021 §12].

Caveats: No provision in the evidence sets a payment day; the question's premise of a settlement date is not supported. Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Under the proposed Immigration Bill, what is the minimum and maximum penalty imposed on a ship's master or aircraft captain who fails to report a transit passenger or crew member that appears to have stayed in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Under the Immigration Bill (082/2026), the fine is "not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than five hundred thousand rupees" [082/2026 §90(2)].

- The duty is to notify an Immigration Officer where a transit passenger or crew member fails to continue the journey, in circumstances from which it may reasonably be inferred the person has remained in Sri Lanka [082/2026 §90(1)].
- Liability falls on the master, captain "or the agent", and is "jointly and severally" on conviction [082/2026 §90(2)].

Caveats: This is the Bill version dated 2026-10-07; the same text appears in 508/2024, 513/2024 and 071/2026. Do not confuse it with §89(3) (fine of 500,000 to 1,000,000 rupees per person) for failing to comply with removal/receiving orders [082/2026 §89(3)].

question: Under the proposed Convention against Doping in Sport amendment, how long does the Board Chairman serve?
answer:
The Chairman of the Board holds office **"for a term of three years"** and is "eligible for reappointment" [636/2025 §11]; the Gazette version is identical [631/2025 §11].

- Appointed by the Minister from the appointed members, on the recommendation of the majority of the ex-officio members [636/2025 §11].
- Text covers the newest Bill (2025-09-12); the earlier GS (2025-09-04) does not differ [631/2025 §11].

Caveats: none; committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Under the amended Rubber Control Act, who is defined as the “Director‑General”?
answer:
Under the amendment, “Director‑General” is defined as “the Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department, appointed or deemed to have been appointed under this Act” [595/2025 §6] (identical text in the newer Bill 620/2025, 2025‑07‑09; GS 595/2025, 2025‑05‑28).

- The clause replaces the old “Controller” definition in section 52 of the Rubber Control Act (Chapter 436) [595/2025 §6].
- Every reference to “Controller”/“Rubber Controller” in other laws, notices, contracts or forms is to be read as “Director‑General of the Rubber Development Department” [595/2025 §2].

Caveats: none; note the 2005 Tea and Rubber Estates bill refers to the same office but is a different Act [008/2005 §5].

question: In the amended Personal Data Protection Act, which bodies are regarded as a public authority?
answer:
The evidence does not contain a definition of "public authority." The definition section of the principal Act [152/2021 §47] defines "controller" as including a "public authority" but never defines the term itself, and the two amendment bills (newest: 591/2025, Bill, 2025-05-08; earlier GS: 575/2025, 2025-03-27) are present only as bill-level outlines and auto-generated summaries, with no clause text on this point.

- Related, but not a definition: §20(1)(a) requires a DPO where processing is by a "ministry, government department or public corporation" [152/2021 §20].
- §28 lets the Minister designate a "public corporation, statutory body or any other institution established by or under any written law and controlled by the government" as the Data Protection Authority [152/2021 §28].

Caveats: The amending clause text may define or amend "public authority," but it is not in the evidence.

question: What criteria does the amendment set for a crop to be classified as an Export Agricultural Crop?
answer:
A crop qualifies if it is "identified as a crop that have an export potential in addition to the local consumption", is not one of the excluded categories, and is declared by the Minister as "a notified agricultural crop" under section 2 [045/2026 §5] (identical text in 060/2026, the newer Bill of 2026-08-07).

- Excluded: "paddy, vegetables, fruits, root crops and additional food crops belonging to the category of food crops" [045/2026 §5].
- Also excluded: "any crop identified as a plantation crop" [045/2026 §5].

Caveats: Citation is to §5 of the GS version (2026-06-25); the Bill version carries the same §5 but no clause text is quoted separately here.

question: Under the proposed Chiththa Advanced Psychological Studies Open Institute of Sri Lanka law, what does the term “qualified auditor” refer to?
answer:
“Qualified auditor” means either an individual accountant or a firm of accountants meeting the stated membership and practising-certificate requirements [597/2025 §10(4)].

- Individual: a member of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of Sri Lanka, or another institute established by law, who “possesses a certiﬁ cate to practice as an Accountant” issued by that Council [597/2025 §10(4)(a)].
- Firm: each resident partner must be such a member and possess that certificate of practice [597/2025 §10(4)(b)].

The evidence says this §10 text is identical in Bill 608/2025 (6 June 2025); the quoted text is from GS 597/2025 (29 May 2025) [597/2025 §10].

question: Under the proposed Proceeds of Crime Bill, what types of advanced investigative methods can an investigation officer employ with a magistrate’s permission?
answer:
Under the Proceeds of Crime Bill, with a Magistrate’s authorization under §56, an investigation officer may use “controlled delivery”; “digital surveillance” including interception/recording of digital, voice and video communications; “undercover operations” including decoys; “laying of traps”; and “forensic extraction” from computers, phones, storage devices and other digital equipment [570/2025 §60].

- The Magistrate must consider “necessity and justification” and proportionality, and may impose conditions [570/2025 §60].
- Progress must be reported “once in fourteen days” [570/2025 §60].

Caveats: the list is from the GS version 570/2025; the evidence says the text is identical in Bill 572/2025 but does not give that Bill’s section number.

question: Under the proposed Chartered Institute of Media Professionals of Sri Lanka law, how many council members must be present, and must the Chairperson be among them, to constitute a quorum for a council meeting?
answer:
Five members, **including the Chairperson**, constitute a quorum for a Council meeting [054/2026 §7(2)]. This is from the Bill titled “Establishment of the Chartered Institute of Media” (2026-07-22); the GS version has identical text [040/2026 §7(2)].

- The Chairperson must be among the five [054/2026 §7(2)].
- Meetings may be held in person or by audio-visual communication if all quorum members can see and hear each other [054/2026 §7(3)(b)].

Caveats: The bill title cited differs slightly from the name in your question.

question: Under the National Transport Commission amendment, what steps must the Commission and transport operators follow to set and show fares for bus and other transport services?
answer:
Under new section 38A, the Commission computes fares by a formula it sets, consistent with the national fare policy approved by Parliament and specified by Gazette Order; it publishes fare lists online, and each operator must adopt those lists and display its fares on the vehicle. [592/2025 §19]

- Formula is "determined by the Commission from time to time", fares to be "specified by Order published in the Gazette". [592/2025 §19]
- Commission publishes the lists on its "official website"; each provider prepares its list accordingly and displays it "at any conspicuous place of the transportation vehicle". [592/2025 §19]
- Commission may inspect compliance; failure is "guilty of an offence under section 40". [592/2025 §19] A related s.8(o) power (2024 bill) requires considering stakeholders' "written representations" and periodic revision. [565/2024 §5]

Caveats: the evidence gives no penalty amount, timeline, or the formula itself. My §5 reference is from the 2024 bill (565/2024), not 592/2025.

question: According to the proposed Mass Foundation law, what continuous legal identity will the foundation have, what ability does it have to bring or face lawsuits, how can it manage its seal, and how is it classified for regulatory oversight?
answer:
Under the Mass Foundation (Incorporation) Bill 037/2026 (2026-05-07; GS 025/2026, 2026-04-08, identical on these clauses), the Foundation has “perpetual succession” and “may sue and be sued” [025/2026 §2].

- Legal identity: perpetual succession under the name “Mass Foundation” [025/2026 §2].
- Seal: full power to “have and use a common seal and to alter the same at its pleasure”; affixation requires two Committee members present and signing independently, and custody lies with a Committee office bearer as decided [025/2026 §2][025/2026 §15].
- Oversight: deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980, whose provisions apply to management [025/2026 §2].

question: Under the amendment to the National Water Supply and Drainage Board Law, when a water supply and sewerage undertaking of an industrial park is transferred to the Board, which minister is treated as the ‘Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government’ for applying Part III of the Act?
answer:
The evidence does state the designation, though ambiguously: for an industrial estate or industrial park, "the Minister in charge of the subject of Local Government" is read as "the Minister assigned the subject of the Board of Investment of Sri Lanka ... or the Minister assigned the subject of industries under Article 44 or 45 of the Constitution" as the case may be [053/2026 §10] (identical text in [019/2026 §10]).

- This is the proviso to the new section 57a, applied when Part III is extended to industrial estate/park and community-based undertakings [053/2026 §10].
- The two bill versions are identical in text; 053/2026 is dated 2026-07-21 and 019/2026 2026-03-13 [053/2026 §10]; [019/2026 §10].
- The community-based organisation case differs, referring to "the Minister assigned the subject of community based water supply" [053/2026 §10].

Caveats: the provision names two alternative ministers and does not say which applies to an industrial park, so the evidence does not resolve the choice.

question: Under the proposed Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill, what responsibilities does a magistrate have when an approved detention centre lies within his jurisdiction?
answer:
Under the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill [078/2026 §33], the Magistrate in whose jurisdiction an approved place of detention sits must, "without giving any advance notice", visit it "once a month", interview the suspects and "look into their well-being", and call for and inspect detention registers, Detention Orders and other documents.

- Torture suspected or alleged: must "forthwith make an order" for production before a Judicial Medical Officer and submission of the report [078/2026 §33(4)]; if satisfied on reasonable grounds, he "shall act in terms of section 31" [078/2026 §33(5)].
- Non-conforming conditions found on inspection must be reported to the Inspector General of Police [078/2026 §34(2)].

Caveats: the earlier Anti Terrorism Bill set a "once a week" visit [444/2024 §32]; the 2026 text says monthly.

question: Under the Mediation (Civil and Commercial Disputes) Bill, which civil or commercial disagreements can be taken to mediation and which types are excluded from this law?
answer:
The Bill applies to “civil and commercial disputes” settled by mediation—whether under a mediation agreement, by voluntary referral, or by court referral [622/2025 §2]. It is Bill 622/2025 (11 July 2025); GS 616/2025 (3 July 2025) has identical §2 text.

- Excluded: disputes required to go through the Mediation Boards Act No. 72 of 1988 or the Mediation (Special Categories of Disputes) Act No. 21 of 2003 [622/2025 §2].
- Also excluded: disputes whose settlement needs terms enforceable only by court decree/order, including the schedule’s categories—e.g. dissolution/nullity of marriage, minors/unsound mind, adoption, partition for rights *in rem*, probate, insolvency, admiralty *in rem*, fundamental rights [622/2025 §3], [622/2025 §30].
- Related matters may still be mediated to submit settlement terms to court [622/2025 §3].

question: What audit regulations govern the financial statements of Samurdhi community‑based banking societies under the Samurdhi amendment?
answer:
For Samurdhi community‑based banking societies, the amendment applies the public‑corporation audit regime: Article 154 of the Constitution and the National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018 govern the audit of their accounts [600/2025 §3]. The new provision is section 35A; the GS version (4 June 2025) and Bill version (17 June 2025) contain identical text [600/2025 §3].

- Article 154’s “provisions … relating to audit of accounts of public corporations” apply [600/2025 §3].
- The “National Audit Act, No. 19 of 2018” also applies [600/2025 §3].
- Section 28A applies the same regime to “samurdhi community based banks,” not societies [600/2025 §2].

question: Under the proposed Companies (Amendment) Act, what remedy is available to a company whose name has been struck off, and what are the effects on its former assets?
answer:
The evidence does address this: on application to court (with the Attorney-General a party) within ten years, the court may permit re-registration and order return of property previously vested in the State [582/2025 §17].

- The company must "show cause to the satisfaction of the court stating reasons why such company was unable to comply" with the relevant provisions [582/2025 §17].
- Third parties who acquired rights in good faith from the State are unaffected, and the State is not liable where property was destroyed, damaged, or never physically taken [582/2025 §17].
- An earlier, near-identical version uses "date of coming into operation of this amendment Act" instead of the 2025 Act reference [541/2024 §15].

Caveats: the text is an amendment to section 487(5) only, not the full section; no passage states the striking-off grounds in subsection (3) or the vesting rule's original wording beyond the quoted substitution.

question: Under the revised Anti‑Corruption Act, in what situations will a person charged with a corruption offence be refused bail?
answer:
The evidence does contain the relevant bail rule — but only as a **proposed amendment** to section 149 of the Anti-Corruption Act, not as the Act's current text.

- Bail may be refused only where the value is certified by the Director-General: a bribe "of not less than one hundred thousand rupees", a Government loss, or a gain/benefit to himself or another "of not less than five hundred thousand rupees"; then the suspect "shall not be granted bail except in exceptional circumstances by a High Court" [051/2026 §17].
- Otherwise all offences are "cognizable and non-bailable as per the provisions of the Bail Act, No. 30 of 1997" [051/2026 §17].
- The presented Bill repeats this but its text is garbled at "offering of section 149 of the principal enactment a bribe" [063/2026 §17].

Currently, s.149 requires remand until trial's end, with bail only in "exceptional circumstances" [311/2023 §149].

Caveats: This is a GS bill of 2026-07-27 and a Bill of 2026-08-19; no in-force amended text is in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters law, how are offences listed in Part B of the extradition schedule treated when Sri Lanka considers extraditing a suspect to another UN member state?
answer:
They are deemed **not** to be political offences: for extradition purposes between Sri Lanka and any UN Member State, an offence in Part B of the Extradition Law's Schedule "shall... be deemed not to be an offence of a political character or an offence connected with a political offence or an offence inspired by political motives" [073/2026 §11].

- This overrides the Extradition Law, No. 8 of 1977 ("Notwithstanding anything in" it) and applies only "for the purposes only of extradition" of an accused or convicted person, or of assistance under section 12 [073/2026 §11].
- The same clause appears identically in the other version, 085/2026 [073/2026 §11].
- Separately, the Schedule is amended to insert, immediately before Part B, "an offence within the meaning of the Prevention of Foreign Terrorist Fighters Act" [073/2026 §8].

Caveats: Both texts are GS (gazette) versions dated 2026-09-30; no presented Bill version is in evidence. The section 12 cross-reference concerns assistance to UN Member States [073/2026 §11], while §12 itself addresses the Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters Act [073/2026 §12].

question: Under the revised National Environmental Act, what monetary penalty does a person face if convicted of an offence covered by Section 23r, and what extra daily charge applies if the violation persists after the conviction?
answer:
Under the amended Section 23r(2), conviction before the Magistrate having jurisdiction carries "a fine not less than one hundred thousand rupees and not more than one million rupees" [032/2026 §18].

- Continuing offence: "a fine of five thousand rupees for each day on which the offence is so continued after conviction" [032/2026 §18].
- This replaces the earlier "ten thousand" to "one hundred thousand" rupees and "five hundred" rupees per day [032/2026 §18].

Caveat: The bill is titled "National Environmental" (Bill, 2026-05-06), not "National Environmental Act"; the quoted text amends the principal enactment.

question: What penalty does the amendment to the National Audit Act impose for the offence covered by Section 42?
answer:
The amendment replaces the existing fine with "a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand rupees or to an imprisonment of either description for a term not exceeding one year or to both such fine and imprisonment" [611/2025 §13].

- It substitutes the former range of "not less than five thousand rupees and not more than twenty five thousand rupees" [611/2025 §13].
- Same text appears in bill 619/2025; the version cited is the Gazette (GS) publication of 23 June 2025 [611/2025 §13].

Caveats: The evidence does not state what offence Section 42 of the National Audit Act No. 19 of 2018 creates, only the penalty substituted.

question: Under the proposed Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs law, what fine and additional action apply if a dog owner does not vaccinate and register the dog after being given a notice?
answer:
Under the bill, the owner is liable to a "penalty of two thousand rupees in addition to the registration fee payable under section 5", and the local authority must itself vaccinate and register the dog in the Register of Dogs ([076/2026 §7(4)]). This appears in both versions with identical text — Bill 076/2026 (presented 2026-09-24) and GS 066/2026 (2026-09-07).

- The notice gives "fourteen days" to vaccinate and register; the officer "may extend the period for further fourteen days" for reasonable cause ([076/2026 §7(2)–(3)]).
- The registration fee is the one prescribed under section 5 ([066/2026 §5(1)]).
- Note the wording is "penalty", not a fine imposed on conviction; the bill's title in both versions is "Elimination of Rabies and Registration of Dogs".

Caveats: Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus; the section-5 fee amount is not stated in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to Sri Lanka’s drug control law, how is the list of named narcotics changed and what new penalty is introduced for manufacturing other listed dangerous drugs?
answer:
The 2026 amendment Bill adds "methamphetamine" to section 54A(1)(a)'s named drugs, and creates a new offence with a fine/imprisonment range for manufacturing other listed drugs [068/2026 §2].

- The list "heroin or cocaine or morphine or opium" becomes "heroin, cocaine, morphine, opium or methamphetamine" [068/2026 §2].
- New paragraph (aa): manufacturing any dangerous drug in Groups A, B, C, D and E of Part I of the Third Schedule, other than those five named drugs, is an offence [068/2026 §2].
- Penalty on conviction by the High Court without a jury: "a fine not less than two hundred thousand rupees and not exceeding five hundred thousand rupees, or to imprisonment ... not less than ten years and not exceeding twenty years, or to both" [068/2026 §2].

Caveats: I rely on the Bill 068/2026 (2026-09-08); the Gazette version 062/2026 (2026-08-24) carries the same text [062/2026 §2].

question: Under the proposed Presidents' Entitlements repeal, will former presidents or their widows keep receiving housing, regular payments, secretarial assistance, official transport or a widow's pension once the new law takes effect?
answer:
No — on commencement those benefits cease: any residence, monthly allowance, secretarial allowance, official transport and other facilities, and the widow's pension provided "in terms of the provisions of section 2 ... section 3 ... section 4 of the repealed Act" "shall no longer be provided with or paid to" [624/2025 §3] (identical text in 627/2025).

- This follows from outright repeal of the Presidents' Entitlements Act, No. 4 of 1986 [624/2025 §2].
- It covers benefits received "preceding the date of commencement" — i.e. existing recipients, including widows of former Presidents [624/2025 §3].

Caveats: Same clause appears in both the GS (624/2025, 2025-07-31) and the Bill (627/2025, 2025-08-07); no commencement date or savings provision is shown in the evidence.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Penal Code, what new penalty is introduced for intentionally causing serious injury to a child under 18?
answer:
The new section 316a imposes up to **10 years’ imprisonment**, plus a fine and possible court-ordered compensation, for “voluntarily causes grievous hurt” to a person under 18 [618/2025 §6] (identical text in Bill 630/2025, 19 Aug 2025; GS 618/2025, 8 Jul 2025).

- The offence is subject to the exception “in the case provided for by section 326” [618/2025 §6].
- Compensation is determined after considering a victim impact statement from the National Authority for the Protection of Victims of Crime and Witnesses [618/2025 §6].

Caveat: the clause says “voluntarily,” not “intentionally”; the evidence does not use “intentionally” for section 316a [618/2025 §6].

question: How does the proposed amendment to the Social Security Contribution Levy Act change the turnover limits and the applicable dates in Section 5, and what new limit is introduced for periods starting on 1 April 2026?
answer:
The amendment in [017/2026 §3] (GS, 2026-03-03; identical text in 023/2026, Bill, 2026-03-17) rewrites s.5(1) by removing "or" from paragraph (b), dating paragraph (c) and adding a new paragraph (d) with a 36 million rupee ceiling for four-quarter turnover from 1 April 2026.

- Paragraph (b): substitutes "hundred and twenty million rupees;" for "hundred and twenty million rupees; or" [017/2026 §3(1)].
- Paragraph (c): substitutes "on or after January 1, 2024 and prior to April 1, 2026," and "sixty million rupees; or" [017/2026 §3(2)].
- New paragraph (d): "for any period commencing on or after April 1, 2026," four consecutive quarters' turnover "does not exceed thirty-six million rupees" [017/2026 §3(3)].

Caveats: Only quoted fragments appear; the full amended limits in s.5(1) and its opening words are not in the evidence.

question: What changes does the amendment to Section 14 of the Sri Lanka Electricity Act make to the ownership percentage requirement and to the type of entities mentioned in its subsections?
answer:
The amendment raises the threshold in Section 14(1) from **"more than fifty per centum"** to **"one hundred per centum"**, and replaces the "person" references in subsections (2) and (3) with a company incorporated under the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007 [584/2025 §12].

- Subsection (1): substitutes **"one hundred per centum"** for **"more than fifty per centum"** [584/2025 §12].
- Subsection (2): **"Any person who"** becomes **"Any company incorporated in terms of the Companies Act, No. 07 of 2007, which"** [584/2025 §12].
- Subsection (3): **"a person who"** becomes **"a company, which"** [584/2025 §12].

Caveats: Evidence is the GS version of the Sri Lanka Electricity (Amendment) bill (2025-05-16), with identical text noted in 599/2025; the section's full text is not reproduced, so the practical scope of the 100% requirement is not shown here.

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Trusts Ordinance, which part of Section 3 is being removed and how is the definition of “express trust” being changed?
answer:
Paragraph (n) of Section 3 of the Trusts Ordinance (Cap. 87) is repealed, and in paragraph (p) the definition of "express trust" has the words "trust generally in the form" replaced by "trust in the form" [081/2026 §2].

- Amendment made by the Trusts (Amendment) - GS bill (GS, 2026-10-14), which states Section 3 was last amended by Act No. 6 of 2018 [081/2026 §2].
- The change is a deletion of "generally", narrowing the wording; the text does not explain its effect [081/2026 §2].

Caveats: The evidence is the Gazette version only, and does not reproduce the full text of paragraphs (n) or (p).

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Judicature Act, how are the retirement ages for judges and magistrates being changed?
answer:
Under the Judicature (Amendment) bill, the retirement age in section 6(3) rises from "sixty-one years" to "sixty-three years", and section 6(4) is replaced so that "the age of retirement of all other Judges and Magistrates shall be sixty-two years" [058/2026 §3].

- The new subsection 6(4) applies "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Public and Judicial Officers (Retirement) Ordinance (Chapter 355)" [058/2026 §3].
- The Bill version (064/2026, 2026-08-18) carries identical text to the GS version (058/2026, 2026-08-07) [058/2026 §3].

Caveats: The evidence does not specify which judges fall under subsection (3) as distinct from "all other Judges and Magistrates".

question: Under the proposed amendment to the Universities Act, how many terms is a person allowed to serve as dean of a faculty?
answer:
A dean may serve **no more than two terms**: "No person shall be appointed as the Dean of a Faculty for more than two terms." [649/2025 §2 (5)]

- This is a new subsection (4) inserted after section 49(3) of the Universities Act No. 16 of 1978 [649/2025 §2].
- The clause text above comes from the GS version (649/2025, gazetted 2025-11-21); the later Bill 655/2025 (presented 2025-12-03) is described as containing the same two-term limit [655/2025].

Caveats: The 655/2025 Bill's clause text is not reproduced in the evidence — only its summary — so the wording is verified only against 649/2025.

question: What 2025 legislation establishes the professional facilities‑management institute as a legal corporate body in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The **Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka (Incorporation)** bill — published as **623/2025 (GS, 18 July 2025)** and presented as **628/2025 (Bill, 6 August 2025)**, whose texts the evidence describes as identical.

- Clause 2(1) provides that members "shall have perpetual succession under the name and style of the 'Institute of Facilities Management Sri Lanka'… may sue and be sued in all courts" with a common seal. [623/2025 §2]
- It succeeds to the Institute's existing debts, liabilities, subscriptions and fees. [623/2025 §3]
- Section 36 defines "IFMSL" as the Institute, "a professional Body established in Sri Lanka". [623/2025 §3]

Caveats: Only an earlier 2024 pair (458/2024 GS; 470/2024 Bill) is otherwise in evidence, with the same clause 2(1) but "Act, No. of 2024" [470/2024 §2]. Committee-stage amendments are not included.
warnings: citations not backed by the retrieved evidence: 470/2024 §2, 623/2025 §2

question: Which 2025 legislation creates a legal corporation for the charitable foundation named after senior monk Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero?
answer:
The Mabotuwana Sri Piyarathana Nayaka Thero Suwasevana Foundation (Incorporation) Bill — Bill 596/2025, presented 2025-05-08 — which constitutes the Foundation's members a body corporate with perpetual succession, power to sue and be sued and a common seal [596/2025 §2].

- Its long title reads "AN ACT TO INCORPORATE THE MABOTUWANA SRI PIYARATHANA NAYAKA THERO SUWASEVANA FOUNDATION" [581/2025].
- The earlier Gazette version, GS 581/2025 (2025-04-10), contains the identical incorporation clause and short title "…Act, No. of 2025" [581/2025 §2]; [596/2025 §1].
- It was presented by Hon. Dayasiri Jayasekara, M.P. for Kurunegala District [596/2025].

Caveats: Only the Bill (596/2025) and its GS precursor (581/2025) are in evidence; no enacted Act number is shown.

question: What 2026 amendment revises the Act that governs marriage and divorce among the Kandyan community (Chapter 113)?
answer:
Bill 016/2026, the Kandyan Marriage and Divorce (Amendment) Bill (presented 2026-02-19; earlier Gazette version 008/2026, 2026-02-05), amends the Kandyan Marriage and Divorce Act (Chapter 113) [016/2026].

- §2 substitutes paragraph (a) of Section 32 with "Adultery by the husband or wife after marrige" [008/2026 §2; identical text in 016/2026].
- §2 also repeals paragraph (b) of Section 32 entirely [008/2026 §2].
- §3 provides that the Sinhala text prevails over the Tamil in any inconsistency [016/2026; 008/2026 §3 heading].

Caveats: No new penalties are stated; the "marrige" spelling appears in the quoted text. Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: What is the 2026 legislation that establishes the Al‑Hashimi Association as a legal corporate entity?
answer:
The Al‑Hashimi Association (Incorporation) Bill — Bill 039/2026, presented 21 May 2026 (earlier Gazette version 024/2026, 8 April 2026).

- It provides that existing and future members "shall have perpetual succession under the name and style of the 'Al-Hashimi Association'" as a body corporate, able to sue, be sued and use a common seal [024/2026 §2(1)].
- The body corporate is deemed a Voluntary Social Service Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980 [024/2026 §2(2)].
- Objects include helping poor people and students, youth self‑employment, fundraising and a trust to manage assets [024/2026 §3].

Caveats: Both versions appear to carry identical clause text; no committee‑stage amendments are in this corpus.

question: Which 2026 bill repeals the 2009 act that created the position of chief of the defence staff in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The Chief of Defence Staff (Repeal) - Bill, Bill 059/2026 (2026-08-04), whose §2 states: "The Chief of Defence Staff Act, No. 35 of 2009 is hereby repealed" [059/2026 §2].

- Identical text also appears in the earlier Gazette version, 036/2026 (GS, 2026-05-15), so the two versions do not differ [036/2026 §2].
- On commencement, the Chief of Defence Staff and Committee members "cease to hold such office" [059/2026 §3(1)].
- Office staff are reassigned to the armed forces, Police, Civil Security or public service; property and liabilities transfer to the Defence Ministry [059/2026 §3(2)].

Caveats: The presented Bill title differs slightly from the question's phrasing; 059/2026 is the version to cite.

question: What 2025 legislation modifies the 1988 Provincial Councils Elections Act in Sri Lanka?
answer:
The 2025 Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Bill amends the Provincial Councils Elections Act, No. 2 of 1988 — GS version 589/2025 (published 2025-05-22), presented as Bill 605/2025 (2025-06-05) [589/2025 §1][605/2025].

- It makes the 1988 Act's provisions "in force on September 21, 2017" operative again, "notwithstanding the amendments made thereto by Act, No. 17 of 2017" [589/2025 §2].
- This takes effect from the date the Amendment Act comes into force, without prejudice to acts done from 22 September 2017 that are not inconsistent with the 1988 Act [589/2025 §2].
- Short title: "Provincial Councils Elections (Amendment) Act, No. of 2025" [589/2025 §1].

Caveats: Only clauses §1–§2 and bill-level summaries appear here; the Sinhala/Tamil inconsistency clause (§3) is listed in the outline but its text is not given. Committee-stage amendments are not in this corpus.

question: Which 2025 bill amends the 2016 Act that provides a financial assistance scheme for workers?
answer:
The **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment)** bill amends the Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers Act, No. 4 of 2016 [602/2025 §2]. The newest version is Bill 602/2025 (presented 2025-06-03); the earlier Gazette version is 587/2025 (2025-05-20) [602/2025] [587/2025].

- It amends s.3 of the 2016 Act to end the allowance periods on "March 31, 2025" [602/2025 §2].
- Deemed to have come into operation on "April 1, 2025" [602/2025 §1].

Caveats: The 2016 Act's own text is not in the evidence; the "financial assistance scheme" description comes from the question, not the passages.

question: Which 2025 bill seeks to amend the 2016 legislation that establishes the minimum wage for employees in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 604/2025, the National Minimum Wage of Workers (Amendment) Bill (3 June 2025), amends the National Minimum Wage of Workers Act, No. 3 of 2016 [604/2025 §2]. Its Gazette predecessor is 586/2025 (20 May 2025) [586/2025 §1].

- It replaces section 3(1): Rs 27,000/month (Rs 1,080/day) from 1 April to 31 December 2025, then Rs 30,000/month (Rs 1,200/day) from 1 January 2026 [604/2025 §2].
- Budgetary relief allowances under the 2005 (No. 36) and 2016 (No. 4) Acts count as part of that minimum wage and are consolidated into pay [604/2025 §3].
- It is deemed to have come into operation on 1 April 2025 [604/2025 §1].

Caveats: The 2024 Bill 537/2024 also amended the same Act (Rs 17,500/700) but is not a 2025 bill [537/2024 §2].

question: Which 2025 amendment alters the 2005 law that established the workers' special financial assistance allowance?
answer:
The **Budgetary Relief Allowance of Workers (Amendment) Bill — 603/2025** (Bill, 3 June 2025; earlier GS version 588/2025, 20 May 2025), which amends Act No. 36 of 2005.

- It substitutes in section 3(1) the words "With effect from August 1, 2005" with "For the period commencing on August 1, 2005 and ending on March 31, 2025" [588/2025 §2].
- No new powers or penalties; the Sinhala text prevails over the Tamil [588/2025 §3].

Caveats: The near-identical 587/2025 amends the *2016* Act (No. 4 of 2016), not the 2005 Act [587/2025 §2]; only the GS text of 588/2025 is quoted in detail.

question: What 2026 legislation proposes to abolish the 1977 law that provided retirement benefits to Sri Lankan parliamentarians?
answer:
The **Parliamentary Pensions (Repeal) Bill** — Bill 001/2026, dated 2026-01-07 — provides that "The Parliamentary Pensions Law, No. 1 of 1977 is hereby repealed" [001/2026 §2].

- Purpose is stated to be repeal, not new powers or penalties [001/2026 bill-level description].
- The bill also appears to address existing pension payments, though the text of §3 is truncated in the evidence [001/2026 outline].
- Sinhala text prevails over Tamil in case of inconsistency [001/2026 §4].

Caveats: The evidence shows this as a Bill (presented), not a Gazette version; §3's wording is cut off, so its exact effect on current pensions cannot be quoted.

question: Which 2025 bill sought to modify the 1988 Sri Lankan law that imposes a tax on gambling activities?
answer:
The **Betting and Gaming Levy (Amendment) Bill** — Bill **642/2025** (presented 2025-10-21), preceded by the Gazette version **640/2025** (2025-10-02) — amends the Betting and Gaming Levy Act, No. 40 of 1988 [640/2025 §2].

- It substitutes rates in section 2(1A): 10% retained, 15% "for any year commencing on or after April 1, 2023 but ending prior to October 1, 2025", and a new 18% rate from 1 October 2025 [640/2025 §2(1)].
- It doubles a specified charge from "United States Dollars fifty" to "one hundred" [640/2025 §2(2)].
- The 1988 Act was "last amended by Act, No. 11 of 2023" [640/2025 §2].

Caveats: Only the GS clause text (640/2025) is in evidence; 642/2025 appears only at bill level, so I cannot confirm whether its clauses differ.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes changes to the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)?
answer:
The 2025 bill is **625/2025, Land Development (Amendment)** (Bill, 2025-07-22), preceded by the Gazette version **617/2025** (GS, 2025-07-04); both are described as being "to amend the Land Development Ordinance (Chapter 464)" [625/2025][617/2025].

- It amends s.48A by repealing "or upon his or her marriage" in 48A 2(c) [625/2025 §2].
- It repeals subsection 48B 1(a) [625/2025 §3].
- It changes s.68(1) from "fails to succeed" to "fails without reasonable cause to succeed" [625/2025 §4].

Caveats: The Chapter 464 reference appears only in the bill-level description/outline, not in the numbered clause text, which says only "the principal enactment"; committee-stage amendments are not covered.

question: Which 2026 bill updates the 2018 Finance Act No. 35?
answer:
The Finance (Amendment) Bill, No. 034/2026 (Bill, 2026-05-06), which amends section 44 of the Finance Act, No. 35 of 2018 [034/2026 §2]. An identical Gazette version was published as 027/2026 (GS, 2026-04-23) [027/2026].

- It inserts a proviso exempting newly constructed cellular towers that commence commercial operations "on or after January 1, 2026" from the levy "for a period of five years" [034/2026 §2(1)].
- It makes the levy payable "Subject to the provisions of subsection (1)" [034/2026 §2(2)].

Caveats: The Inland Revenue (Amendment) GS 013/2026 also mentions the 2018 Act, but only to write off interest on debt repayment levy, not to amend it [013/2026 §45].

question: Which 2026 bill revises the 1956 law that sets rules for female workers, teenage employees and child labor?
answer:
Bill 056/2026, the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children (Amendment) Bill (presented 2026-07-22), amends the Employment of Women, Young Persons and Children Act, No. 47 of 1956 [056/2026 §2].

- It substitutes "one hundred thousand rupees" for "ten thousand rupees" in sections 7(3), 13(2) and 20a(3) [056/2026 §2][056/2026 §3][056/2026 §4].
- The higher amounts do not apply to offences committed before the Act comes into operation [056/2026 §5].
- The same text appears in the earlier Gazette version, 044/2026 (GS, 2026-06-25) [044/2026].

Caveats: The title matches the question; the auto-generated summaries are hints only, so details above come from the clause text.

question: Which 2025 bill proposes to revoke the 2024 legislation that introduced internet safety and content regulation measures?
answer:
Bill 590/2025, the **Online Safety (Repeal)** Bill (presented 2025-05-08), repeals the Online Safety Act, No. 9 of 2024 [590/2025 §2]. An earlier Gazette version, 578/2025 (2025-04-08), contains identical repeal text [578/2025 §2].

- It also repeals any regulations made under the 2024 Act, "from the date of enactment of this Act" [590/2025 §3].
- Short title: "Online Safety (Repeal) Act, No. of 2025" [590/2025 §1].
- No new powers, duties or penalties are introduced — the bill only nullifies the earlier law and its rules [578/2025, bill-level description].

Caveats: The 2024 Act's own content is not in the evidence, so "internet safety and content regulation" is inferred from the auto-generated summary, not clause text.

question: What 2025 legislation addresses re‑conducting postponed local council elections by allowing new nominations and setting a fresh election date?
answer:
The **Local Authorities Elections (Special Provisions) Bill** — Bill **566/2025** (presented 2025-01-09), whose published Gazette version is **565/2025** (GS, 2025-01-01). The two versions' clause text is identical in the evidence.

- It deems earlier nomination papers for the postponed 9 March 2023 elections "of no force and effect as if such nomination papers had never been submitted", and revokes the published nomination notices [565/2025 §2(1)–(2)].
- Fresh nomination notices under s.26 of the Local Authorities Elections Ordinance must be gazetted on a date the Election Commission determines, "not later than three months from the date of coming into operation of this Act" [565/2025 §3].
- Deposits are refunded on production of the s.29(3) receipt [565/2025 §2(3)].

Caveats: the Act's operative citation and the specific poll date are not shown in the evidence; only the three-month limit for nomination notices appears.

question: Which 2025 bill updates the 2008 act that governs major strategic development projects in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 650/2025, the **Strategic Development Projects (Amendment) Bill** (presented 2025-11-14), amends the Strategic Development Projects Act, No. 14 of 2008, "as last amended by Act, No. 12 of 2011" [650/2025 §2]. Its Gazette predecessor is 643/2025 (GS, 2025-11-07), with identical clause text [643/2025].

- It substitutes "ten years." for "twenty-five years." in the proviso to section 2 [650/2025 §2].
- It repeals and replaces section 3, requiring the BOI to refer projects to the Ministry of Finance for ex-ante cost-benefit analysis, with a recommendation "within one month" [650/2025 §3(3)].

Caveats: Only clause extracts are in evidence; the auto-generated summaries' mention of ex-post monitoring, penalties and tax returns is partly supported by [650/2025 §4] but not fully verifiable here.

question: Which 2026 bill was introduced to legally establish the UnV charitable foundation?
answer:
The **UnV Foundation (Incorporation) Bill — Bill 010/2026, dated 22 January 2026** — is the 2026 bill to incorporate the UnV Foundation [010/2026 §1] [010/2026].

- It was presented by Hon. Imran Maharoof, M.P. [010/2026].

- Its long title is “An Act to incorporate the UnV Foundation” [010/2026].

question: Which 2025 bill updates Sri Lanka's 1979 criminal procedure legislation?
answer:
The 2025 update is the **Code of Criminal Procedure (Amendment)** published as Gazette bill **576/2025** on 2025-03-28, which amends the Code of Criminal Procedure Act, No. 15 of 1979 [576/2025 §2]; identical text also appears in 579/2025 [576/2025 §5].

- Inserts sections 144A–144B letting a Magistrate dispense with a suspect's or accused's personal attendance in court in specified circumstances [576/2025 §2].
- Inserts sections 273A–273U on taking evidence through "contemporaneous audio-visual linkage" [576/2025 §5].
- Amends the Second Schedule by adding Forms 24 and 25 for commissions served abroad [576/2025 §6].

Caveats: the evidence covers only the Gazette ("GS") version, not a presented Bill; and both 576/2025 and 579/2025 are described as carrying the same text.

question: What 2026 bill proposes the twenty‑second revision of Sri Lanka’s constitution?
answer:
Bill 065/2026, the **Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution** (Bill, 18 August 2026), presented by the Minister of Justice and National Integration; its earlier Gazette version is 057/2026 (GS, 7 August 2026).

- It repeals and replaces Article 107(5): Supreme Court judges retire at "sixty-seven years", Court of Appeal judges at "sixty-five years", and the Chief Justice at 67 or after six years in office, "whichever occurs earlier" [065/2026 §2].
- It amends Article 137, substituting "not more than twenty four other Judges" for "not more than nineteen other Judges" [065/2026 §3].
- Short title: "This Act may be cited as the Twenty Second Amendment to the Constitution" [065/2026 §1].

Caveats: Older bills with the same title (e.g. 460/2024, 493/2024) amend different Articles; the auto-summary for 065/2026 misdescribes the retirement age as unchanged.

question: Which 2026 bill seeks to repeal the 1972 Tenancy Act (No. 7) in Sri Lanka?
answer:
Bill 006/2026, the **Rent (Repeal) Bill** (Bill, 2026-01-20), is the 2026 bill that repeals Act No. 7 of 1972 — though the Act it names is the **Rent Act**, not a "Tenancy Act": "The Rent Act, No. 7 of 1972 is hereby repealed" [006/2026 §2].

- Repeal is clause 2; the short title is the "Rent (Repeal) Act, No. of 2026" [006/2026 §2].
- Transitional protections last "a period of one year from the relevant date" — no ejectment suits and no rent above the "authorised rent" [006/2026 §3(a)–(b)].
- Pending Rent Board and Board of Review matters must be concluded within that same one-year period [006/2026 §3(d)–(e)].

Caveats: If you meant a differently titled "Tenancy Act" bill, no such bill appears in this evidence; the summary details are auto-generated hints only.

question: What 2026 legislation creates a corporate entity for the Mahawilachchiya children’s education centre?
answer:
Bill **015/2026 — Mahawilachchiya Education Centre for Children (Incorporation)**, presented 18 Feb 2026; its Gazette version was **011/2026**, dated 6 Feb 2026. [015/2026] [011/2026]

- It converts existing Centre members into a body corporate with perpetual succession, power to sue/be sued and a common seal. [011/2026 §2]
- It deems the body corporate a Voluntary Social Services Organization under Act No. 31 of 1980. [011/2026 §2]

Caveat: §2(1) names the corporation “Mahawilachchiya Centre for Education for Children,” slightly differently from the bill title; the evidence shows Bill/GS text, not an enacted Act. [011/2026 §2]
